info.title: Permguard health, version and keys
info.description: Plane health and version, the telemetry listener's probes and the key-set endpoints. Both planes serve the same paths on their own ports.

200.description: Plane and product; build details only when disclosed. Both planes answer.

get.x-grpc-note: The data plane answers the same document over permguard.data.v1.DataPlane/GetInfo (identical GetInfoResponse).
Same body as `/`; the data plane answers over permguard.data.v1.DataPlane/GetInfo.

get.summary: The plane's liveness, readiness and lifecycle phase
get.description: Always 200; the state is in the body. Both planes carry the lifecycle: the plane's `state`, what it serves without in `degraded`, and every component the process hosts in `components`, a plane not yet Ready listed with its phase rather than omitted.

200.description: The health of the plane asked.

get.x-grpc-note: The data plane answers over permguard.data.v1.DataPlane/GetHealth with the same members.
Telemetry listener probe; no gRPC counterpart.
Telemetry listener probe; no gRPC counterpart.

get.description: Always 200, even when the process reports itself unhealthy.
get.x-grpc-note: Prometheus text exposition on the telemetry listener; no gRPC counterpart.

get.summary: The control plane public keys as a JWKS

200.description: The key set; an empty set when nothing is published.

503.description: The ring cannot be read; plain text, never an empty set.

get.x-grpc-note: The response carries the JWKS as JSON bytes (`GetKeyRingResponse.jwks`).

get.summary: The data plane public keys as a JWKS

200.description: The key set; an empty set when nothing is published.

503.description: The ring cannot be read; plain text, never an empty set.

get.x-grpc-note: The data plane serves no key-ring RPC (permguard.data.v1 has none); keys are HTTP-only there.

get.summary: The Server Host operations ring public keys as a JWKS

200.description: The key set, when no Host listener a verifier can reach is configured; an empty set when nothing is published.

308.description: A Host listener over plain TLS is configured: the ring is served there. `308` keeps the method, so a verifier follows as the same `GET`.

Deprecation.description: `true`, the boolean form of the HTTP Deprecation header's draft (RFC 9745 later made the value a date): this route is legacy.

503.description: The ring cannot be read; plain text, never an empty set.

get.x-grpc-note: The telemetry listener has no gRPC. The ring's Host API counterpart is `permguard.host.v1.KeyService/GetKeyRing`, served by the Host listener and described in `host.json`; this endpoint redirects to its REST path once a Host listener is configured.
get.description: The legacy route of the operations ring. Without a Host listener (`admin.addr`), or with one that demands a client certificate, it publishes the ring; with a Host listener over plain TLS it answers `308 Permanent Redirect` to that listener's `/host/v1/keys/host.operations`, the place the process registry's `jwks_uri` then names, and publishes nothing itself (WP-2.5).

plane.description: The plane's id as configuration spells it.

version.description: Empty when the deployment does not disclose builds.

commit.description: Empty when the deployment does not disclose builds.

InfoBody.description: What `/` and `/version` answer on a plane.
InfoBody.x-grpc-note: The data plane's permguard.data.v1.GetInfoResponse has the same four fields.

component.description: `server-host`: the Host is not a plane.

version.description: Empty when the deployment does not disclose builds.

commit.description: Empty when the deployment does not disclose builds.

VersionBody.description: What the telemetry listener's `/version` answers (`VersionBody`, permguard-telemetry).
VersionBody.x-grpc-note: The telemetry listener's `/version` is REST-only: the Server Host is not a plane and has no gRPC counterpart.

capability.description: The capability's name, as the configuration calls it.

reason.description: Why, in the terms an operator would fix it in.

Degraded.description: One capability that is served and cannot currently do its work.
Degraded.x-grpc-note: The data plane's permguard.data.v1.Degraded has the same two fields.

component.description: The component's name: `host`, a plane's id, or a service's name.

state.description: A lifecycle phase for the Host and a plane; `disabled`, `running`, `backoff`, `draining` or `failed` for a service.

required.description: Whether the component gates readiness: the Host always, a plane unless `runtime.optional_planes` names it, a service never.

stalled_since.description: Since when it cannot progress for a remote reason. Absent when it can.

last_success.description: A service's last successful run. Absent when it had none, or for the Host and a plane.

next_attempt.description: When a service in backoff tries again. Absent otherwise.

reason.description: Why it is where it is: the failure, the backoff, what it waits for. Absent when nothing is wrong.

Component.description: One component of the process, as `components[]` lists it.
Component.x-grpc-note: The data plane's permguard.data.v1.Component has the same fields.

degraded.description: Capabilities this plane serves without. Absent when empty.

components.description: Every component the process hosts: the Host first, then every configured plane, then the services. A plane not yet Ready is listed with its phase, never omitted.

degraded.description: Capabilities this plane serves without. Absent when empty.

components.description: Every component the process hosts: the Host first, then every configured plane, then the services. A plane not yet Ready is listed with its phase, never omitted.
